commits.subject: fix(shadow): bypass production-lock short-circuit in shadow pipeline
commits.body:
select_pick short-circuits and returns the loaded production DailyPick
when production is already locked (game started or bluesky_posted=True).
This is correct for the production cascade but wrong for the shadow
cascade: _run_shadow_prediction was calling the same select_pick with
shadow predictions, so when shadow ran after production locked, the
function discarded the shadow predictions and returned production's
DailyPick. save_shadow_pick then wrote production's data to
{date}.shadow.json, silently masking every disagreement as "AGREES" in
the eval.

Repro on 2026-04-12: production picked Brendan Donovan (SEA) 71.7%, but
the real shadow top was Nico Hoerner (CHC) 70.5% with Steven Kwan (CLE)
69.8% double-down — a real DISAGREES day that the bug converted to
AGREES, and 2026-04-12.shadow.json was byte-identical to the production
file (same run_time microseconds).

Fix: add for_shadow=False parameter to select_pick; when True, skip the
production-lock short-circuit so the shadow always computes its own pick
from its own predictions. Scheduler's _run_shadow_prediction now passes
for_shadow=True.

Tests:
- test_strategy::test_for_shadow_ignores_locked_production — unit test
  showing the bypass behavior at the strategy layer
- test_shadow_scheduler::test_writes_independent_shadow_file_when_production_locked
  — integration test using the REAL select_pick (not mocked). Catches
  this class of bug in the future; the existing tests mocked select_pick
  entirely which is why the bug was invisible to CI

Why 4/10 and 4/11 escaped: 4/10 shadow file was written by Eric's manual
verification of commit 8c900c8 (production was on pre-shadow-wiring
scheduler). 4/11 was written by Fly running in shadow_mode=true where
save_pick wrote bluesky_posted=False, so the short-circuit couldn't
fire. 4/12 was the first end-to-end Hetzner run with the normal-post
flow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: refactor(picks): load_shadow_pick honors bluesky_posted on disk
commits.body:
Previously load_shadow_pick force-overrode bluesky_posted=False and
bluesky_uri=None on every load, regardless of what was in the file. That
was a secondary masking layer for the select_pick short-circuit bug
(634768e): the corrupted shadow file written with production's
bluesky_posted=True would silently have that field reset to False on the
next check-results save-back, hiding the evidence of corruption.

Now that the root cause is fixed, the load should be honest — if a
shadow file ever shows bluesky_posted=True again, it means something
upstream is wrong and we want to see it on disk immediately.

Normal operation is unchanged: shadow files are written with
bluesky_posted=False and stay False. Only corrupted files behave
differently, which is the point.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
